Alex: Heads up, saw streaming users report "stuttering" between token chunks after last microbatch change.
Maya: Which metric moved? p95/p99? Any kernel changes?
Alex: p95 steady, p99 up. Canary numbers:
```
p95=90ms
p99=340ms
throughput=760tokens/s
kernel=fused-attn-kv
kv_hit_ratio=72%
hotspots=kernel_sync_wait, kv_reencode
```
Jamal: Context: we increased default microbatch from 2->6 and stream chunk from 6->18. Fewer flushes, bigger chunks.
Sophia: That improves throughput but increases perceived latency per token (users see longer gaps). Fused kernel gives better avg but worse tail when KV churn occurs.
Liam: Also saw dynamic kernel switch path: if seq_len crosses threshold we reselect kernel mid-request -> forces a sync -> big tail spike.
Alex: So tradeoff: throughput vs token-level perceived latency. Need experiments + short-term mitigation.
Maya: Proposed small experiment grid (same model/hw):
- microbatch_size: 1,3,6
- stream_chunk_tokens: 4,12,20
- flush_interval_ms: 25,70,140
Measure p50/p95/p99 token latency, inter-chunk gap, t/s, kernel_choice, kv_hit_ratio.
Jamal: Quick canary runs (3 combos):
- mb=1 chunk=4 flush=25 -> p99=120ms t/s=530 kernel=base kv_hit=88%
- mb=3 chunk=12 flush=70 -> p99=280ms t/s=740 kernel=fused-attn-kv kv_hit=75%
- mb=6 chunk=20 flush=140 -> p99=500ms t/s=920 kernel=fused-attn-kv kv_hit=70%
Sophia: Nonlinear tail growth with chunk/flush. UX pause approximates flush_interval + kernel tail.
Maya: Short-term mitigations:
1) Cap streaming chunk tokens for latency-tier clients.
2) Force low-tail kernel for streaming path (even if avg lower).
3) Adaptive flush heuristic to break big microbatches when tail risk high.
Sophia: Example adaptive heuristic (pseudo):
```
if predicted_kernel_high_tail or kv_hit_ratio < 0.8:
  effective_chunk = min(chunk_tokens, 8)
  if time_since_last_chunk > flush_threshold: flush()
else:
  wait(min(flush_interval_ms, max_batch_wait))
```
Jamal: Canaryed adaptive flush + prefer-base-kernel for streaming: middle combo p99 dropped 280->140ms, throughput -6%.
perf-bot: perf-regression-alert commit abc123 increased hosted streaming p99 by +60ms on canary (adaptive flush deployed to mitigate). https://perf/reports/abc123
infra-bot: Rolling canary 10% for 2h with extra tracing tags: trace=stream_chunk,kv_hits,kernel_choice
Alex: Good. Maya, can you open a ticket with the experiment matrix, traces, and recommend defaults? My SDK doc update: default stream_chunk_tokens=8, flush_interval_ms=40, microbatch_cap=3 for latency SLO.
Maya: Will do and attach traces. Also add note to runtime: avoid mid-request kernel reselect or warm the alternative kernel early.
Liam: Long-term: kernel selection policy should consider tail risk and streaming semantics; also precompile warm kernels on ramp-up.
Alex: Assigning follow-ups. Closing for now. :thumbsup:
